text.p: German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG said on Wednesday that it would link with Canada's Bombardier Inc to set up a charter firm for business jets in the second quarter of 1997.

In a statement, Lufthansa said the supervisory board of its Lufthansa CityLine GmbH unit had approved the move at a meeting on Tuesday December 3. Both companies had signed a joint venture agreement on November 20, Lufthansa said.
The firm will start operations in Berlin next year.
The company will provide business service aircraft for charter throughout Europe.
Lufthansa said the venture would enable it to expand its service for European and American business travellers, giving them access to destinations not covered by scheduled flights.

"The extension of our capacity by a Lear and Challenger fleet from Bombardier will allow us to serve the growing demands of business travellers," Lufthansa CityLine managing director Karl-Friedrich Rausch said.
Lufthansa CityLine, a 100 percent subsidiary of Lufthansa, currently runs flights throughout Europe using aircraft with fewer than 100 seats.
The unit had 28 Canadair jets, 15 Avro RJ85 and three Fokker 50 aircraft at the end of 1996, but will use only the jets from April 1997, Lufthansa said.
